Folks — quick read-through and high-level positions:

1) Liability cap: Corelytics' $1M ask is below our standard for ISV marketplace integrations. Proposed Redwood position: capped at the greater of $2,000,000 or 2x the trailing 12-month fees (excluding any amounts paid for professional services). We will except carveouts for gross negligence and will not accept IP indemnity carveouts without very specific factual basis.

2) Data flow & retention: we will accept a 30-day default retention for logs but need flexibility to extend for compliance incidents with prior notice and approval. KMS: Redwood is willing to support customer-managed encryption keys (KMS) for production workloads; need to specify which environments and escrow/rotation expectations.

3) Audit & breach support: recommend adding a clause for SOC2 attestation access and a 30-day SLA for providing requested logs in the event of a security incident. We should avoid open-ended e-discovery commitments.

4) SOW acceptance criteria: request explicit test cases (3 integration test flows) and an acceptance signoff milestone before go-live. This helps procurement and PS planning.

I've attached our annotated suggestions inline. If Corelytics can move to 1.75M we may have room to compromise during partner pricing / marketplace placement.

Attachment: [attachment: RI_annotated_redlines_v1.docx (docx)]

I can join a call Thursday 8/5 at 09:30 PT if that works for Corelytics.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference

Ben / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and Laura for the detailed comments. A few notes from Corelytics' side following an internal review: 

- Liability cap: our legal and procurement teams prefer a fixed cap. Based on budget constraints we can move from $1M to $1.5M, but we need IP indemnity to stay in scope and limited carveouts for security incidents.
- Data Flow Annex: CISO wants explicit language on PII tokenization and a hard 30-day rolling retention for logs. They are open to a short exception process for investigations.
- KMS: we cannot do customer-managed keys in the short term; we need Redwood to confirm encryption-at-rest with vendor-managed keys and provide key rotation schedule.

Attached: [attachment: Corelytics_MSA_redline_v3.docx (docx)] — this reflects the $1.5M cap and a tightened annex.
